page: Microsoft Azure E96bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 96 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running on Intel processors under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 768.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio to accommodate expansive memory working sets without requiring distributed clustering. Direct-attached local storage is provided via 5,669 GB of NVMe SSD space, and the system is engineered to interface with Azure Premium Storage for high-throughput remote block storage workloads. The configuration does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

The inclusion of 5,669 GB of integrated NVMe SSD media allows high-bandwidth scratch space and low-latency local caching directly on the host hypervisor. Trade-offs are characterized by the standard virtualization configuration, where advanced vector extensions are not exposed to the guest OS. In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the high concentration of RAM and direct-attached storage reduces multi-instance sprawl for workloads constrained primarily by memory capacity and disk I/O.

Microsoft Azure E96bds_v6 is best aligned with large relational database engines, in-memory operational data stores, distributed caching systems, enterprise resource planning platforms, and intensive extract, transform, and load operations requiring large local buffers.
description: Microsoft Azure E96bds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by Intel processors and 768.0 GB of system RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance incorporates 5,669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Premium Storage block volumes, while omitting dedicated GPU acceleration. The large memory capacity combined with high-density local NVMe storage reduces network storage dependency for high-throughput caching and staging workloads. Resource allocation favors memory and storage capacity over specialized hardware accelerators, representing an efficient single-node footprint for consolidating memory-intensive enterprise tasks without multi-instance clustering overhead. Consequently, the E96bds_v6 is engineered for large-scale relational database engines, in-memory data analytics, caching tiers, enterprise transaction processing, and ETL workloads that require substantial memory capacity coupled with fast local scratch disks.
